transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

I... well, I'm here because of the voices. I keep hearing them. It's like someone is right there in my studio with me. They say my name. They tell me my work is being judged. But... it's quiet. Nobody else is there.
Have you also been feeling unusually depressed or unusually high or energized when the voices happen?

I don't know about depressed. But... I guess I had a lot of energy. 

I was... well, I was only sleeping a few hours a night. I was just pushing these big plans I had. For my art, and my care work. And... yeah, the voices were happening in the studio then, too. I just... I felt certain people were watching my work.
How long have you been hearing the voices?
Um... a while. I guess... maybe about nine months now. Yeah, about nine months. Just... hearing them. And being so sure people are watching my work.
Have these experiences made it harder for you to work or take care of yourself?

I guess... yeah, it has. I almost lost my job as an aide. I was missing shifts and... I just couldn't keep my care notes straight anymore. Everything got so disorganized. And... I stopped going to my walking club. I used to go to these art talks at the library, but I stopped doing that, too. I've just been staying home by myself mostly.
During this time, have you had a period of at least a week when you felt abnormally elated or overly irritable?

I suppose so. It's... well, sometimes I just feel so bright. Like I'm chosen for something, and all my plans are just too big for Greenville to hold. But then... I don't know. I guess I can get pretty snappy, too. Just... snapping hard at people over little things. Like if one of my clients asks me to repeat myself, I just... I get so irritated. I don't mean to, it just happens.
Have you ever heard the voices or felt watched when you were not having those high-energy or irritable periods?

Yes. Um... there was a time. After my energy kind of dropped back down. I was sleeping more normally again, but... the voices were still there. And I still felt like people were tracking what I was doing at work. That went on for... a few weeks, I think. Even when I wasn't feeling so high or irritable.
Have there been any times when the voices or the feeling that people were watching you lasted for at least two weeks while your mood was otherwise normal?

I... I think I just mentioned that. Yeah. After my energy dropped back down and I was sleeping normally again... it kept going for several weeks. The voices. And feeling like people were judging or tracking my work... it lasted for a few weeks like that.
During your high-energy times, did you ever need to be hospitalized?
No. I... I haven't been hospitalized for it.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview confirms prominent psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations and persecutory/reference delusions) lasting about 9 months, with a clearly documented period of at least 2 weeks of psychotic symptoms persisting after mood returned to baseline. There was also a syndromal manic episode with decreased need for sleep, increased energy, expansive/grandiose ideas, irritability, and functional decline. Because psychotic symptoms occurred outside mood episodes and the overall course includes manic symptoms rather than only depression, the best fit is schizoaffective disorder, bipolar type.
